detail: Between 5% and 10% below the high counts as a pullback, and the S&P 500 closed at 7,201.09 on Tuesday, about 7.9% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October, after a 0.5% dip. It has now fallen on eight of the last nine trading days, a reminder that recoveries rarely go in a straight line.
source: Reuters closing figures via StreetInsider, 24 Nov; record close from Anadolu and EdgeX, 6 Oct

detail: Breadth was mixed on Tuesday: on the Nasdaq 2,376 shares rose and 2,548 fell, roughly even, though 323 hit new 52-week lows against 49 new highs. Selling was deep in chip and AI shares while healthcare and shops rose, so the damage was concentrated rather than market-wide.
source: Reuters closing breadth via StreetInsider, 24 Nov

detail: Above 4.5% counts as high, and the US 10-year yield edged down to about 4.90% on Tuesday ahead of today's inflation figures. Safe bonds paying close to 5% still set a high bar for shares to beat.

Markets expect rates to go up: CME FedWatch put the chance of a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December at about 97% on Tuesday, with about a 66% chance of another in January, and markets price about an 80% chance of a Bank of England rise on 17 December. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and tend to weigh on share prices, especially fast-growing companies.
source: CME FedWatch via Reuters, 24 Nov; RateProbability OIS pricing, 25 Nov

detail: Above $90 a barrel counts as expensive, and Brent crude rose 2.3% to settle at $91.40 on Tuesday, back over that line after more tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz. Dearer oil feeds into fuel and transport costs, which can keep inflation and interest rates higher for longer.
source: ICE settlement via Bloomberg (Rigzone) and Investrade, 24 Nov
